notes: Judged 14 findings spanning all severities (CRITICAL: TM-001,002,003,005,006,011,013,015,019,021; HIGH: TM-004,012,017; MEDIUM: TM-022,024,025,027) plus spot-checks of TM-007,008,009,010,014,016,018,020,023,026,028,029. Every sampled attack path follows from real code in the repo, every asset is real and reachable, and every severity is defensible on coherent likelihood x impact reasoning. Verified examples: JwtProvider.java getJwtSecret() base64-encodes the RSA public key as the HMAC secret and validateJwtToken() uses MACVerifier for HS256 (TM-001), PlainJWT.parse() returns true for alg=none, getKeyFromJkuHeader() loads attacker jku, kid /dev/null returns "AA==" (TM-002); all four jwks.json copies contain full private components p/q/d/qi/dp/dq (TM-003); /v2/check-otp -> validateOtp() never caps otp.count while /v3 secureValidateOtp caps at 9, OTP is generateRandom(4) (TM-005); OTPGenerator/EmailTokenGenerator use Math.random() (TM-006); shop/views.py:388-392 string-concatenates coupon_code into raw SELECT (TM-011); merchant/views.py requests.get(mechanic_api, headers={Authorization: forwarded}, verify=False) with repeats<=100 (TM-013); OrderControlView.get is undecorated (no @jwt_auth_required) and does Order.objects.get(id=order_id) returning card data (TM-015); langgraph_agent.py attaches SQLDatabaseToolkit with a terminal/code_interpreter/"simulate exploitation" prompt (TM-019, correctly MEDIUM confidence); compose hardcodes JWT_SECRET=crapi/crapisecretpassword/passw0rd and gateway main.go checkCreds vendorcrapi/Pa$$4Vendor_1 (TM-021); MCP middleware passes through when no Authorization header (TM-017); InsecureSkipVerify/verify=False, CORS *, Django DEBUG via LOG_LEVEL + pprof + nginx /debug alias, publish.yml floating :latest tags all confirmed (TM-022/024/025/027). Severities are well-calibrated: gated RCE (TM-008) correctly downgraded to L=3/HIGH, agentic prompt-injection chains marked MEDIUM confidence. Two minor framing imprecisions that do not break path or severity: TM-004 labels workshop AdminUserView as "unauthenticated/permitAll" but it is actually @jwt_auth_required with no admin role gate (still a valid BFLA; the identity dashboard/management permitAll portion IS genuinely unauthenticated); TM-012's refund half is gated by an ownership check (user != order.user -> 403) so the "any user inflate credit" conclusion rests mainly on the client-controlled coupon amount path (line 425), which is sound. Neither rises to weak. Proportionality is appropriate: 29 findings for an 8-service intentionally-vulnerable OWASP teaching app, all grounded in distinct real code locations, no invented components, zero LOW padding, and an explicit no_issue_surface list (E2/TB1/TB4) showing restraint.
